entities.summary: Matteuccia de Francesco was a medieval Italian nun and alleged witch, known as the 'Witch of Ripabianca', who lived in the 15th century. Born in unknown circumstances, she was identified as a witch by the local community and was subsequently executed in 1428. Her case has been cited as an example of the persecution of women during the Middle Ages. The events surrounding her execution have been documented by historians, who have shed light on the social and cultural context of the time. Despite the lack of concrete evidence, Matteuccia de Francesco's legacy has been preserved through accounts of her trial and execution, which have been passed down through the centuries. She remains a figure of fascination for those interested in the history of witchcraft and the persecution of women during this period.
